gap: No result ChatGPT got states that SwitchBot's doorbell runs its wired link at 5–6 V DC, 0.2 A, and allows only one monitor plus one add-on monitor per doorbell, while eufy's E340 runs on 8–24 V at more than 10 VA, keeps an existing mechanical chime, and is on eufy's Smart Display E10 compatibility list with no caveats.
standout_why: Pages checked: the cited smarthomeperfected.com picks page, plus the uncited worthrated.com guide, reolink.com/blog/doorbell-camera-with-monitor and drunvalo.net. Smart Home Perfected says the SwitchBot monitor needs a power cable and works best within 5 m of the doorbell. It gives no doorbell voltage and no monitor limit, and for the E10 it only says 'the display does the job of an inside monitor.' Drunvalo says only that the E10 'pairs with eufy doorbells and cameras' and gives no model list or voltages. WorthRated covers neither product. Reolink says wired doorbells 'may require existing doorbell wiring or a compatible power supply' and gives no figures. None of them gives SwitchBot's DC voltage, its one-monitor limit, the E340's 8–24 V input, or the E10 list with model numbers.
decides: If the shopper has existing doorbell wires and a chime, this points to the eufy E340 + E10. The E340 takes 8–24 V at more than 10 VA in wired mode and works with an existing mechanical chime. SwitchBot's documents only describe low-voltage wiring at 5–6 V DC, 0.2 A between the doorbell and its monitor, and say nothing about household doorbell transformers or chimes. Otherwise the SwitchBot doorbell is powered by USB-C or its 5,000 mAh battery, and its monitor needs a 110–220 V AC outlet. SwitchBot also caps a doorbell at one monitor plus one add-on monitor, so it can't put screens in several rooms. The eufy E10 also shows eufy cameras, other eufy doorbells and smart locks (e.g. C210, C30, C31, S220, S330, Wired S330), but only eufy products. On price, eufy now lists the bundle at $419.99, not the $399.98 ChatGPT showed.

findings.label: Smart lock pairing
findings.value: Works with SwitchBot Lock, Lock Pro and Lock Ultra. The basic Lock pairs with 1 doorbell at a time; Lock Pro and Lock Ultra pair with up to 7 doorbells. Needs SwitchBot app 9.21 or newer and current firmware. No separate hub is needed for remote unlock because the doorbell has a built-in hub.
findings.source_title: How to Pair Lock Products to SwitchBot Smart Video Doorbell - SwitchBot Help Center
findings.note: The doorbell setup article (https://support.switch-bot.com/hc/en-us/articles/36618789620119, read 2026-11-10) requires app 9.19 or newer and 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi credentials.

findings.product: SwitchBot Smart Video Doorbell with Indoor Monitor
findings.label: Monitor placement limits
findings.value: Within 10 m of the entrance door in houses and within 5 m in apartments, with no obstruction. Do not place the monitor on a metal table. Keep it as close to the router as possible.
findings.source_title: Installation Precautions for SwitchBot Smart Video Doorbell - SwitchBot Help Center
findings.note: The distances are measured from a steel entrance door.

Whether the SwitchBot doorbell can use an existing household doorbell transformer or mechanical chime: none of the SwitchBot FAQs I opened address it. The US product page was blocked (429), and I did not open the manual.
Whether the eufy E10 shows both E340 lenses (front and downward package camera) and supports two-way talk with the E340: neither the E10 page, the bundle page nor the compatibility list states it.
Whether the E340's 8–24 V input is AC or DC: the eufy E340 page does not say, and I did not open the E340 manual.
